alice_support: FYI customer reported that when their app triggers two tool calls in parallel (search + run_sql) the tool_results sometimes swap — search result ends up attributed to run_sql and vice-versa. Happening ~5% of requests, higher under load. INC-1234 opened.

raj_oncall: Can you paste the minimal repro and any correlation IDs they saw?

alice_support: Repro steps they gave: 1) POST /v1/chat with function_calls: [search, run_sql] 2) both calls configured as async 3) client waits for 'tool_result' events, then maps by tool.name but observes wrong mapping.

alice_support: Example snippets from their logs (sanitized):
```
request_id=rc_9a1b2c
correlation_id=cor_42
tools_fanout=[search:callid=call_111, run_sql:callid=call_112]
received_tool_result: {"tool":"search","callid":"call_112", "output":"..."}
received_tool_result: {"tool":"run_sql","callid":"call_111", "output":"..."}
```

ingmar_dev: This looks like a tool_result <-> original request association bug. Two hypotheses: 1) correlation header reused across parallel subcalls and we use arrival order to map, 2) a dispatch queue that de-queues out-of-order and rewrites the tool->call mapping.

lina_sre: Deploy-bot posted a deploy to `eng-runtime` last night at 2026-03-15 02:14 UTC; see digest below — any new batching/async fanout changes?
deploy-bot: Deployed eng-runtime v2.14.0 (batching/async refactor). CI: green.

ingmar_dev: OK I can repro locally with a small script that fires two parallel tool invocations against the runtime. Minimal repro (node):
```
await Promise.all([
  fetch('/internal/toolcall', {headers:{'x-rdwd-cor': 'cor_42'}, body: JSON.stringify({tool:'search', callid:'call_111'})}),
  fetch('/internal/toolcall', {headers:{'x-rdwd-cor': 'cor_42'}, body: JSON.stringify({tool:'run_sql', callid:'call_112'})})
])
```
I see tool_results arrive with swapped callids about 1/20 runs.

raj_oncall: Any logs showing the internal correlation id used by runtime? We need the queue trace.

ingmar_dev: Found log traces: worker-7 dequeue msg.id=msg_555 -> maps to callid call_111, forwards to tool runtime, but when result returns it tags result with msg.parent_id rather than original callid if parent_id is present. When two messages share same parent_id (the correlation header), the external callid can be overwritten.

lina_sre: That points to the async refactor where we introduced `parent_id` as the correlation key to group fanout. Looks like we accidentally dedup/merge metadata for messages with identical parent_id.

alice_support: Customer impacted also flagged unexpected billing: two tool calls charged to single ticket and sometimes credits misapplied. Billing-bot any idea?
billing-bot: Noted billing anomalies tied to INC-1234. If callids are swapped at attribution time, usage attribution can mislabel tokens. We should pause auto-invoicing for that account until we patch.

ingmar_dev: Quick mitigation: treat per-tool callid as source-of-truth for attribution and attach a unique fanout_index header (x-rdwd-fanout-index) on each parallel subcall so parent_id is not the only key. I'll push a hotfix to ensure metadata merging uses (parent_id, fanout_index) tuple.

raj_oncall: Steps I'll take now:
- Patch runtime to avoid mutating callid on result path (hotfix branch: fix/fanout-metadata-2171)
- Add temporary guard to prefer explicit callid in incoming tool_result payloads for mapping
- Roll hotfix to staging and run customer repro 1k iterations
- If green, schedule canary to prod in 30m

ingmar_dev: Confirmed tests: local 10k runs -> zero swaps after hotfix. Pushing PR now.

alice_support: Customer updated: we'll run canary and follow up in 2 hours. Also assigning billing review and refund window if necessary.

lina_sre: Added an alert to paging rule if tool_result mapping errors exceed 0.5% for any tenant.

alice_support: Notes for the ticket for postmortem: root cause = metadata merge on parallel fanout using only parent_id; fix = include per-subcall index and prefer explicit callid for mapping; mitigations = billing pause, canary rollout, alerting.

raj_oncall: I'll keep the thread updated. Thanks all :thumbsup:
